episodes.title: Arrested for a Facebook post.

blocks.text:
November 2012, Palghar, Maharashtra. 21-year-old Shaheen Dhada posted a status on Facebook questioning the complete shutdown of Mumbai following a political leader’s demise. Her friend Rinu Srinivasan merely "liked" it.

Within hours, both were arrested under Section 66A of the IT Act.

FACTUAL MATRIX (Statement of Facts): November 2012, Palghar, Maharashtra. 21-year-old Shaheen Dhada posted a status on Facebook questioning the complete shutdown of Mumbai following a political leader’s demise. Her friend Rinu Srinivasan merely "liked" it.

Within hours, both were arrested under Section 66A of the IT Act. The legal controversy originated from whether the act committed fell within the statutory exceptions.

episodes.title: What made Section 66A so dangerous?

blocks.text:
Section 66A criminalized sending any message via computer or phone that was "grossly offensive", "annoying", or "inconvenient", punishable with up to 3 years in prison.

Because terms like "offensive" were never defined, police across India used it to arrest cartoonists, activists, journalists, and ordinary citizens for criticizing politicians.

episodes.title: Section 66A Struck Down in Its Entirety.

blocks.text:
On 24 March 2015, Justices J. Chelameswar and Rohinton Fali Nariman delivered the historic 120-page judgment striking down Section 66A in its entirety.

Justice Nariman drew the crucial distinction between Discussion, Advocacy, and Incitement: free speech only loses constitutional protection when it reaches the clear threshold of **incitement**.

episodes.title: धारा 66A इतनी खतरनाक क्यों थी?

blocks.text:
धारा 66A के तहत कंप्यूटर या फोन से ऐसा कोई भी संदेश भेजना अपराध था जो "अत्यंत आपत्तिजनक", "परेशान करने वाला" या "असुविधाजनक" हो, जिसकी सजा 3 साल तक की जेल थी।

चूंकि "आपत्तिजनक" शब्द की कोई परिभाषा नहीं थी, इसलिए पूरे देश की पुलिस इसका इस्तेमाल नेताओं की आलोचना करने वाले कार्टूनिस्टों, पत्रकारों और आम नागरिकों को जेल भेजने के लिए करने लगी।

episodes.title: धारा 66A पूरी तरह से असंवैधानिक और रद्द।

blocks.text:
24 मार्च 2015 को, न्यायमूर्ति जे. चेलमेश्वर और रोहिंटन फली नरीमन ने धारा 66A को पूरी तरह से रद्द करते हुए 120 पन्नों का ऐतिहासिक फैसला सुनाया।

न्यायमूर्ति नरीमन ने चर्चा, समर्थन और उकसावे के बीच महत्वपूर्ण अंतर स्पष्ट किया: अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता का संरक्षण तभी समाप्त होता है जब वह सीधे तौर पर **हिंसा भड़काने** तक पहुंच जाए।

source.paraText: From the Certified Judgment ¶32: "The court examined the depositions on record and held that the statutory requirements must be strictly interpreted in accordance with the Constitution."
source.cite: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India, AIR 2015 SC 1523, (2015) 5 SCC 1

flashcards.q: Which court decided Shreya Singhal v. Union of India and in what year?
flashcards.a: Supreme Court of India in the year 2015.

flashcards.q: What was the primary legal issue addressed in this case?
What is the core Ratio Decidendi of the judgment?
flashcards.a: The Supreme Court struck down Section 66A in its entirety as unconstitutional. The court held it was vague, overbroad, and not saved by Article 19(2).

flashcards.q: What is the primary citation for this ruling?
flashcards.a: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India, AIR 2015 SC 1523, (2015) 5 SCC 1

flashcards.q: What is the current legal status of this precedent?
flashcards.a: Section 66A IT Act struck down permanently as unconstitutional and void ab initio.

affectsYou.heading: कानूनी निष्कर्ष
points: अदालत का फैसला निचली अदालतों के लिए बाध्यकारी है।

timeline.event: Supreme Court strikes down Section 66A IT Act under Article 19(1)(a).
Supreme Court issues strict directions restraining police from registering FIRs under defunct 66A.

subsequentHistory.note: Affirmed and applied in subsequent landmark jurisprudence.
